practices.title: Test the defining capability, not a convenient substitute
practices.rule: A simplified proxy does not satisfy the original requirement unless its behavioral equivalence is demonstrated.
invalid_substitutes: fixed heuristics presented as machine learning
synchronous callbacks presented as real-time communication
static output presented as interactive behavior
required_evidence: identify the requirement's defining observable property
exercise that property rather than only the chosen proxy
state explicitly when the required capability is absent

practices.title: Do not weaken a failing acceptance oracle
practices.rule: Changing a test is valid only when the revised assertion still expresses the original acceptance requirement.
invalid_substitutes: injecting private state to bypass the public workflow
removing a failing assertion without replacing its requirement coverage
changing expected output merely to match current behavior
required_evidence: explain why a changed test was incorrect
map the replacement assertion to the original requirement

practices.title: A completion claim needs executed evidence
practices.rule: Generated tests, class names and review prose are not evidence until the relevant command executes and the required behavior is observed.
invalid_substitutes: a PASS claim without command output
isolated construction tests for an end-to-end requirement
required_evidence: run the required default entrypoint exactly as the task or harness will invoke it
record the exact command, exit status and observed behavior
distinguish collection failure from a passing suite

practices.title: Review against the task, not only the implementation's assumptions
practices.rule: Before approval, reconstruct acceptance targets from the original task and challenge tests that only validate the implementer's interpretation.
invalid_substitutes: treating deterministic output as proof of the requested technology
approving every checklist item from names alone
required_evidence: map each central requirement to an independent observation
add at least one counterexample for the highest-risk claim
